mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC, from -16.4% to -14.9%, indicates a gradual recovery in consumer spending that will continue to drive retail and recreation mobility higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in WORKPLACES mobility below -20% signals a reduction in office attendance and associated weekday retail activity, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases despite WORKPLACES remaining below -20% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high (above 3%) while WORKPLACES mobility stays low (below -20%), it indicates a persistent work-from-home trend, reducing spontaneous retail visits and driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high and WORKPLACES mobility remains low.

mechanism_narrative: In a low mobility environment, persistent low TRANSIT station activity (below -10%) indicates reduced overall movement within the metropolitan area, which directly limits foot traffic to retail and recreation venues over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days increases significantly despite TRANSIT remaining below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in GROCERY_PHARM mobility below 0% for two consecutive weeks would signal increased public caution or reduced essential outings, which would spill over to discretionary retail, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days increases or remains stable despite GROCERY_PHARM falling below 0% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If the slight recovery in RETAIL_REC is accompanied by a concurrent upward trend in TRANSIT mobility (e.g., above -15%), it suggests a broader return to urban activity and public transport use, boosting RETAIL_REC further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC shows weekly increase and TRANSIT rises above -15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases despite both RETAIL_REC and TRANSIT showing an upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent negative values in WORKPLACES (around -20%) and TRANSIT (around -14%) indicate a continued subdued level of overall economic and commuter activity, which will constrain any significant recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly increases (e.g., by more than 5 percentage points) despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining at their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: As mid-November marks the beginning of the pre-holiday shopping season, consumer behavior shifts towards increased retail and recreation visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks, irrespective of other mobility patterns.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases or remains stagnant, indicating no seasonal uplift for holiday shopping.
